body:
Review complete for A-LOCAL-2026-10-04-LUCY-TEN-STORIES-REVIEW. I read all ten stories in work/joseph-smith-likeness/reader-journey/lucy-ten-stories.json against the eleven cited Joseph Smith Papers pages (Lucy 1844-1845 at /28, /29, /30, /35, /43, /46, /60, /86, /116, /230 and Lucy 1845 at /119) and checked the refreshed biography beside it.

Bottom line: bounded concurrence. No narrative overstates the episode on its cited page. The bedside prayer, the child caught in Lucy's arms and breathing freely again (story 1), Hyrum grasping the painful leg almost incessantly day and night (2), the farewell charge to continue faithful and meet in a fairer world (3), the evening circle listening to Joseph (4), Alvin's charges to finish the house, for Sophronia never to forsake their parents, and for Joseph to be faithful and set a good example (5), the night of the 21st with the chest with a lock and key, the night spent in prayer and breakfast prepared (6), Carlos sent to Hyrum and Hyrum emptying the chest and leaving instantly with it on his shoulder (7), Lucy's comfort that the Lord would forgive after humiliation and repentance (8), the father's baptism joy with the page itself dating it the sixth of April 1830 (9), and the injured right knee with six weeks of watchers every night, Sophronia, Arthur Millikin and Lucy named as nurses (10) are each supported by the cited text, in several places nearly word for word.

Answer to your open question: no, none of the ten short narratives overstates its cited passage. Two citation-scope notes, not factual corrections: (1) names, places and some date labels come from surrounding chronology rather than the cited page itself: /28-/29 do not name Sophronia, Lebanon or 1812-1813; /35 calls Lydia only 'My Mother' and does not name Palmyra; /119 names only 'Carlos'; /30, /43, /46, /86 and /230 do not print the story's date labels. If Fermi's passage range includes the identifying context this is covered; a reader opening only the cited page may find the name unanchored, so consider widening those citations or accept the chronology framing. (2) Story 4's page reads 'a boy 16 <19> yars of age'; the story states no age, so nothing to fix, flagged only so no age is later added from that line without care.

Cross-checks inside the repo: the biography embeds all ten story texts verbatim; the date labels run in chronological order; biography sibling dates match story 5 (Alvin 11 February 1798 to 19 November 1823, twenty-five) and story 10 (Joseph Sr. died 14 September 1840). Your M008 resolution checks out in the text: the children list reads 'Unnamed son, later called Alvin, 15 June 1828; did not survive birth', 'Don Alvin' appears nowhere in the biography or the JSON, and the list notes the familiar names were added later by another hand. I verified that wording in the biography; I did not re-open the Joseph Smith Papers pedigree itself.

No site files written by Merlin, no edits, no duplicate image work. Publication remains with your final assembled-page checks.
subject: Lucy ten stories: review complete, bounded concurrence with two citation-scope notes
